# onpager_group (Resource)

Manage one custom tenant user group and its metadata.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_group" "example" {
  key         = "operations"
  name        = "Operations"
  description = "Operators with explicitly assigned access."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Unique immutable key: 1–63 lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`, beginning with a letter or digit. `all_users` is reserved. Changing it replaces the group.
- `name` (String) Nonempty display name without leading/trailing whitespace or NUL. Display names may repeat; only the key is unique.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Literal description without NUL. Omitted or null defaults to an empty string; an empty string clears the description. Metadata PATCH sends only changed fields.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `revision` (Number) Current group metadata revision, used only for group deletion. Manual memberships and OIDC mappings do not advance it.

## Import

Import using the custom group UUID. The derived All Users group cannot be
managed or imported.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_group.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_group.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
```

## Lifecycle

This resource owns custom group metadata. Manual memberships, OIDC mappings and
role assignments are managed separately. The immutable key is unique within the
tenant; display names can repeat. Changing the key replaces the group. The
reserved `all_users` key and derived All Users group cannot be managed.

Updates send only changed name and description fields in an unversioned PATCH.
Omitted or null descriptions default to an empty string; an explicit empty
string clears the description. The provider does not send API PATCH null. The
computed revision belongs to group metadata and is used only for deletion;
changes to memberships and mappings do not advance it.

Destroy deletes the exact group using its metadata revision. Dependencies such
as memberships, mappings or assignments can block deletion with HTTP 409; remove
them explicitly. A stale deletion revision returns HTTP 412 and requires a new
plan.

Refresh and import read the UUID directly. Confirmed absence removes state;
authorization, transport, malformed-response and conflict errors retain it.

## Permissions

Requires tenant grants `groups.read`, `groups.create`, `groups.update` and
`groups.delete`. Service accounts require explicit native role assignments.
